Pillar Taxonomy Guide

Last updated 2026-06-14 · 1 min read
pillars taxonomy aml markets science

How AcaciaFund organizes research into three thematic pillars, with criteria for classification and examples.

AML — Anti-Money Laundering

AspectDetail
ColorAmber (#d97706)
IconShield
ScopeFinancial crime detection, regulatory compliance, sanctions enforcement, crypto regulation, cross-border financial intelligence
Key SourcesFinCEN, FATF, OFAC, EU Commission, national regulators, compliance technology vendors
Example Tagsaml, compliance, regtech, financial-crime, sanctions, kyc, transaction-monitoring

Markets — Markets & Industry

AspectDetail
ColorGreen (#22c55e)
IconChart
ScopeSemiconductor manufacturing, supply chain dynamics, AI hardware investment, EV battery production, quantum computing VC, industrial policy
Key SourcesIndustry reports, earnings calls, trade publications, patent filings, venture capital data, government industrial policy documents
Example Tagsmarkets, semiconductors, supply-chain, manufacturing, ev, batteries, venture-capital, deep-tech

Science — Science & Discovery

AspectDetail
ColorPurple (#a855f7)
IconMicroscope
ScopeGene editing (CRISPR), protein structure prediction (AlphaFold), exoplanet atmospheres (JWST), brain-computer interfaces, superconductivity, quantum computing science
Key SourcesNature, Science, arXiv (quant-bio, quant-ph), PubMed, NIH, NASA, university press releases
Example Tagsscience, biology, physics, neuroscience, space, crispr, proteins, exoplanets, bci

Cross-Pillar Topics

Some topics span multiple pillars. Notable cross-pillar themes include:

  • Crypto & Blockchain — AML (regulatory enforcement), Markets (investment, mining economics), Science (consensus mechanisms, cryptographic research)
  • AI Regulation — AML (compliance automation), Markets (AI industry investment), Science (AI research, neural networks)
  • Supply Chain Intelligence — AML (trade-based money laundering), Markets (semiconductor/EV supply chains), Science (materials science, logistics optimization)
  • Data Engineering Infrastructure — common underpinning for all three pillars, covered in the DataOps knowledge base
